messages.subject: Discussion about the automated survey design, GIS and MCDS
parts:
Dear DISTANCE colleagues,

I am Mr Ganga Ram Regmi from Nepal and currently a student at Oxford Brookes
University. I am planning to carry out the project entitiled "Estimating
Group Density of Assamese macaque *Macaca assamensis* using Multiple
Covariate Distance Sampling in Lower Kanchenjungha Area, Eastern Nepal".
The study area is steep and consists of 1500 m asl to 3600 m asl in
elevation and unprotected fragmented community forest patches. I am very new
for Distance. I want to design my project with automated survey design
available in distance but no idea how GIS part works in distance. I also
want to know what type of GIS data of my study area (Eastern Nepal) are
required for automated survey design.

Sincerely,
Ganga

messages.author: 12f269733c6eb9a2
messages.subject: Re: Discussion about the automated survey design, GIS and MCDS
parts:
Ganga:

The best way to become acquainted with how Distance in general, and the
survey design engine in particular, is to work through the examples
provided in the Users Guide.

Chapter 3 of the Users Guide entitled 'Getting Started' describes 2
examples of how to use Distance to design a survey. The second example
describes a sample project that comes with Distance "Mexico.dst". You
can examine the files contained in that sample project as well as
"StAndrewsBay.dst" to discover the nature of the GIS shape files needed
to design a survey.

Chapter 6 provides more details about the survey design engine. Work
through the examples and see if they answer your questions.
